new_value: All four fetchers now hold a clock rather than a timestamp. TimeSource is the trait, SystemClock reads the OS clock, and a crate-private Clock enum carries the three cases so the public types keep their shape (HttpCrlFetcher<F, V>, not <F, V, T>) and new() stays const. new(.., now_unix) is unchanged in signature and meaning but now documents what it freezes; with_system_clock reads per check; with_time_source takes a consumer's clock. Each check samples once before the per-URL loop so candidate URLs in one check share an instant. SystemClock reports 0 for a pre-1970 clock, which puts now before every CRL's thisUpdate and so fails closed via CrlExpired. tests/clock_advances.rs contrasts the constructors against a CRL valid through 2026: pinned never sees it expire, clock-driven does; the system-clock test compares against a fetcher pinned to the time the test reads, so it does not depend on the date it runs on. mod time is gated on any(crl, ocsp) -- caught by the feature powerset, not the default build.
